reason: The cited evidence (E1-E3) demonstrates LCO evolution and its effects on dislocation slip and work hardening only under cryogenic conditions and prior thermomechanical processing, not under room-temperature cyclic loading. The key premise that room-temperature cyclic loading induces LCO is unsupported, and the claimed link between LCO and reduced stacking fault energy is not directly evidenced.
premises: Cyclic loading at room temperature induces interstitial-driven LCO domains in FCC CoCrFeMnNi.
LCO domains locally reduce stacking fault energy.
Reduced stacking fault energy promotes dislocation cross-slip.
Enhanced cross-slip delays strain localization and sustains work hardening.
This mechanism operates under moderate plastic strains at room temperature.
